Fortress location detail: native text construction (source extraction)

Source images are the reference and classic PE images configured in
data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. The two saved renderer disassemblies are
reference-render.asm and classic-render.asm. Native literal loads, including
instruction RVAs and literal RVAs for both editions, are recorded in
native-literal-sources.tsv. This file records source semantics; it is not a
test, a game-observation result, or an assertion about an observed game frame.

Renderer boundaries and address notation
----------------------------------------
reference: RVA 0x3b13d0..0x3b90e9; jump tables 0x3b90ec..0x3b926c.
classic:   corresponding renderer instructions are reference RVA - 0x2440.
All instruction references below use reference RVAs unless stated otherwise.
The absolute image base in the saved objdump output is 0x140000000.
The display emits strings through text renderer RVA 0xad9960. Rows containing
labels, values, and punctuation can use several separate calls. A screen row
is therefore not necessarily one source string or one translation key.

The renderer dispatches by the location object's virtual type:
  2 = temple; 8 = tavern; 9 = library; 11 = guildhall; 13 = hospital.
The temple detail branch starts at 0x3b690c; it rejoins the shared personnel
list at 0x3b7c02. Temple-specific source text must include the shared header,
visitor policy, and shared personnel paths in addition to this branch.

Shared name and type header
---------------------------
0x3b179b calls location.virtual(+0x10) to obtain its language_name.
If the name exists and byte +0x72 is nonzero, 0x3b17fc calls the native
language-name formatter (RVA 0xa946e0) with capitalized=true and final=false.
The resulting dynamic name is drawn at 0x3b1887. It is shortened to available
width by the native code, with the final three available bytes changed to
literal '.' when there is sufficient room (0x3b1827..0x3b186b).
This is a generated language name, not a finite English literal list.

Temple type header, 0x3b1d98..0x3b1e71:
  location.+0x16c == 0 -> "Shrine"
  location.+0x16c == 1 -> "Temple"
  location.+0x16c == 2 -> "Temple complex"

Temple religion/deity header, 0x3b1eac..0x3b1fca:
  if location.+0xb8 == 1:
      entity = find_entity(location.+0xbc)            # RVA 0x7daf0
      if entity:
          source = format_language_name(entity.+0x20, true, false)
          native_name_case_helper(source)             # RVA 0x52d650
      else:
          source = "No particular deity"
  else if location.+0xb8 == 0:
      historical_figure = find_hf(location.+0xbc)      # RVA 0x67dc0
      if historical_figure:
          source = "Dedicated to "
          source += format_language_name(hf.+0x38, true, false)
      else:
          source = "No particular deity"
  else:
      source = "No particular deity"
  draw(source)

The organized-religion branch supplies its generated name directly; it does
not prepend "Dedicated to ". The deity branch prepends that literal.

Other type headers in the same renderer are "Hospital", "Library", "Tavern",
and a generated profession descriptor followed by " meeting place",
" guildhall", or " grand guildhall". The guild header also constructs
"<count> member[s]", ", no members", "No established guild",
"<count> worker[s]", and ", no workers". These are sibling type branches,
not additional temple states.

Shared visitor policy
---------------------
0x3b22db..0x3b2332 reads location flag bits in priority order:
  flag bit 6 -> members policy
  otherwise flag bit 4 -> all visitors
  otherwise flag bit 5 -> citizens plus long-term residents
  otherwise -> citizens only

0x3b2695..0x3b27ed draws exactly one of:
  members policy and type == 11:
      "Only members can visit (if guild established)"
  members policy and any other supported type:
      "Only members can visit"
  all visitors:
      "All visitors welcome"
  citizens plus long-term residents:
      "Citizens and long-term residents only"
  citizens only:
      "Citizens only"

The members button is exposed for guildhalls and for temples whose
location.+0xb8 == 1 (0x3b233c..0x3b236e). The visitor icons are texture draws;
they do not replace or supply the visitor policy string.

Temple value and next-rank line
------------------------------
0x3b690c calls RVA 0xe64560; its result minus one is passed as the native
value-format option to helper RVA 0x77f920. The detail data is the object returned by
location.virtual(+0x18), saved in renderer local [rbp-0x58].

if detail exists:
    current_value = native_value_format(detail.+0x38, native_option - 1)
    switch detail.+0x34:
        2: source = "Temple Complex, " + current_value
        1: source = "Temple, " + current_value
           source += " (next at "
           source += integer(global RVA 0x239a1bc)
           source += byte(0x0f)
           source += ")"
        0: source = "Shrine, " + current_value
           source += " (next at "
           source += integer(global RVA 0x239a1b8)
           source += byte(0x0f)
           source += ")"
    draw(source)                                     # 0x3b6aab

The value helper can supply an approximate value, such as "~3000" plus the
native money glyph. The next-rank value is formatted as an integer, then the
money glyph byte 0x0f is appended explicitly at 0x3b6a85. This value, money
glyph, and next-rank clause are meaningful source content and must survive
translation. "Temple Complex, " uses title case in this line while the upper
type header uses "Temple complex".

Complete native money-value helper
----------------------------------
The helper disassemblies are saved as reference-value.asm and classic-value.asm.
reference RVA 0x77f920..0x77fb92 includes both the initial unwind body and its
continuation at 0x77fa58; the continuation must not be mistaken for a separate
text builder. The corresponding classic range is 0x77d340..0x77d5b4.

currency = byte(0x0f)                                # native CP437 money glyph
if native_option <= -1:
    return "?" + currency                            # unknown value
if native_option >= 15:
    return integer(signed_value) + currency           # exact signed value

For option 0..14 the helper takes abs(signed_value), retains a negative flag,
and chooses a native threshold through its jump table. Immediate threshold
arms are 10000, 5000, 4000, 3000, 2500, 2000, 1500, 1000, 500, 200, 100,
50, 25, and 10; the initially cleared threshold also supplies zero.
if absolute_value <= threshold:
    return integer(absolute_value) + currency
    # This native early return uses the absolute amount without reinserting
    # its saved sign; translation retains the actual source output.

rounding_boundary = threshold + 50
if absolute_value <= rounding_boundary:
    amount = round_to_nearest_10(absolute_value), with minimum amount 10
    approximate_prefix = "~"
else if absolute_value <= 3 * rounding_boundary:
    amount = round_to_nearest_100(absolute_value), with minimum amount 100
    approximate_prefix = "~"
else if absolute_value <= 30 * rounding_boundary:
    amount = round_to_nearest_1000(absolute_value), with minimum amount 1000
    approximate_prefix = "~"
else:
    amount = 30 * rounding_boundary + 500
    approximate_prefix = ""
    append_uncertainty_suffix = true

source = approximate_prefix
if signed_value < 0: source += "-"
source += integer(amount)
source += currency
if append_uncertainty_suffix: source += "?"
return source

The source union therefore includes unknown "?" plus currency, exact integer
plus currency, approximate "~" plus integer plus currency, their native signed
forms, and very uncertain amounts with a trailing "?" after the currency.
This helper supplies no English nouns. A complete translation of the temple
rank line must preserve these source value forms and the money glyph rather
than accepting only the photographed "~3000" amount.

Temple worshipper count
-----------------------
0x3b6ac4 obtains count = RVA 0x2a6e00(location.+0xb8, location.+0xbc).
  count > 0 -> format_integer(count)                  # 0x3b6b12
  count <= 0 -> "No"                                 # 0x3b6b35
The renderer then draws a separate " " and:
  count == 1 -> "worshipper"
  otherwise -> "worshippers"
Thus the possible row grammar is:
  "No worshippers"
  "1 worshipper"
  "<integer other than 1> worshippers"
The count and noun use distinct draw calls; translating only one physical
fragment is not complete coverage of the constructed row.

Priest recognition, requirements, and agreements
------------------------------------------------
0x3b6be9 tests whether the location has an organized religion (+0xb8 == 1).
If it does not, the branch displays:
  "Only organized religions can have recognized priesthoods."
If the religion lookup is absent, the branch omits further recognition text.

For an organized religion with a valid entity:
  recognized_rank = 0
  for each position in entity.+0x10c0:
      match position token "PRIEST" or "HIGH_PRIEST"
      inspect entity assignments at +0x1110
      retain assignments whose position id matches position.+0x20 and whose
      site id equals the current site global RVA 0x2393674
      matching PRIEST -> recognized_rank at least 1
      matching HIGH_PRIEST -> recognized_rank at least 2

"PRIEST" and "HIGH_PRIEST" (loads at 0x3b6c79 and 0x3b6d55) are internal
position tokens used for comparisons, not user-facing text labels.

if detail.+0x34 > recognized_rank:
    search the current agreements for the matching organized religion
    if an applicable agreement exists, the recognition action is available
    otherwise:
        required_count = global RVA 0x239a1c0 when recognized_rank == 0
                         global RVA 0x239a1c4 when recognized_rank == 1
        if worshipper_count < required_count:
            source = recognized_rank == 0 ? "Priest: " : "High priest: "
            source += integer(required_count)
            source += " worshipper"
            if required_count != 1: source += "s"
            source += " needed"
            draw(source)
        else:
            draw(recognized_rank == 0 ? "Recognize priesthood"
                                     : "Recognize high priest")
else if detail.+0x34 == 0:
    draw("You can recognize a priesthood once this is a temple.")
else if detail.+0x34 == 1:
    draw("You can recognize a high priest when this is a temple complex.")

For current agreements of type 0x0c that match the religion, if the agreed
rank exceeds detail.+0x34:
  agreed rank 1 -> "Agreed to build temple"
  agreed rank 2 -> "Agreed to build temple complex"
The renderer only searches these build-agreement messages while the current
detail rank is at most 1 (0x3b713d..0x3b741d).

All recognition explanations, both button captions, both agreement captions,
both singular/plural requirement rows, and the non-organized-religion state
are part of the temple detail's source grammar. They are not mutually
replaceable with the one explanation visible in the supplied screenshot.

Temple common-area rows
-----------------------
Chests: 0x3b748c..0x3b7677 counts item type 0x0a within eligible common-area
building contents. The label and value are drawn separately:
  "Chests in common area: " + integer(chest_count)
If no detail object exists, the count is zero.

Stored instruments: 0x3b77a3..0x3b799a, only when a detail object exists:
  "Stored Instruments (Desired): " + integer(detail.+0x40)
  + " (" + desired_field + ")"
  desired_field = integer(detail.+0x0c) normally
  desired_field = screen.+0x88 text while that value is actively edited
  the active field also draws "_" or " " as a blinking cursor
The cursor changes by the native tick value modulo 2000 and threshold 1000.
These number fields and cursor calls are separate from the label call.

Dance floor: 0x3b7ad4..0x3b7bef:
  draw("Dance floor in common area: ")
  width = screen.+0x10; height = screen.+0x14
  if width > 0 and height > 0:
      draw(integer(width) + "x" + integer(height))
  else:
      draw("None")
The positive dimensions remain meaningful even when either dimension is
less than 5; only native display color differs.

The temple branch has no "Rented rooms (Total): " row. That row belongs to
the tavern sibling branch at 0x3b6847..0x3b68d7.

Shared personnel and position rows
----------------------------------
0x3b7c02..0x3b903f iterates the screen's combined personnel vectors in their
native order. Each row is three native cell rows high. The renderer is shared
between location types, so its complete fixed title union is:
  "Tavern Keeper"
  "Performer"
  "Scholar"
  "Scribe"
  "Mercenary"
  "Monster Slayer"
  "Doctor"
  "Diagnostician"
  "Surgeon"
  "Bone Doctor"
Their load instructions are 0x3b7edb, 0x3b7fc9, 0x3b7ff6, 0x3b8023,
0x3b8050, 0x3b807d, 0x3b80aa, 0x3b80d7, 0x3b8104, and 0x3b8131.

A null entry in screen.+0x20 follows the generated position-title path:
  entry = screen.+0x50[index]                         # 0x3b8166
  source = copy(entry.+0x98 string)                   # 0x3b816e..0x3b8179
  title_case(source)                                 # RVA 0x52d3c0
  draw(source)                                       # 0x3b8199
This title is dynamic. The screenshot's "Sacred Turquoise" is not a hardcoded
renderer literal and must not be reduced to a one-title vocabulary patch.
Its upstream generated-position construction is a separate source helper
dependency; see the generated priest-title notes appended below.

Assigned person name, 0x3b7f41..0x3b8250:
  for ordinary role entries:
      find current unit using entry.+0x0c, unless that id == -1
      if a current unit exists:
          source = unit_name_helper(unit, option=false)  # RVA 0x1330c30
      if source is empty and entry.+0x08 != -1:
          use historical figure entry.+0x08
  for generated position entries:
      assignment = screen.+0x68[index]
      if assignment.+0x04 != -1:
          find current unit from this historical-figure id
          if present: source = unit_name_helper(unit, false)
          if source is empty: use the same historical figure id
  historical-figure fallback:
      name = hf.+0x38
      identity = hf_identity_lookup(hf)                # RVA 0xc0f630
      if identity:
          name = identity_name_lookup(identity)        # RVA 0xc3a4f0
      source = format_name(name)                       # RVA 0xa94030

The assigned name is drawn at 0x3b84db after native truncation with a final
ellipsis when needed (0x3b847d..0x3b84bf). A missing assignment can leave the
name field empty; the role or generated position title still exists.
The remaining calls in 0x3b825e..0x3b900b draw portrait, affiliation, role,
assignment, and remove buttons from native texture ids. They do not add
additional English literals to the static text renderer's source stream.

Generated priest-position title dependency
------------------------------------------
The shared position layout and native selection paths are already documented
in data/extracted/character-header-profession-decompiled.txt:
  neutral singular title +0x98
  female singular title +0xd8
  male singular title +0x118
  neutral/female/male plural titles +0x158/+0x198/+0x1d8
The detail's empty-position row copies the neutral singular title +0x98;
assigned-unit name/profession helpers may select the other native variants.

Existing generated priest vocabulary is derived by
tools/legends_grammar.py::religious_name_nouns from installed
data/vanilla/vanilla_languages/objects/language_words.txt WORD/NOUN forms,
with data/runtime/procedural-word-senses.tsv as the WORD-aware noun meanings.
Both singular and plural noun spellings are retained. For homonymous English
nouns, the existing procedural name default is reused only if that default
matches a reviewed noun sense; unrelated generic UI/verb meanings are not
substituted into generated religious titles.

The existing data/runtime/legends-events.tsv religious-prefix entries supply
the complete native ordinary/highest-priest prefix family:
  high         -> 高阶
  first        -> 第一
  exalted      -> 高尚
  holy         -> 神圣
  sacred       -> 神圣
  most high    -> 至高
  absolute     -> 绝对
  most exalted -> 至尊
  most holy    -> 至圣
  most sacred  -> 至圣
The existing compiler combines each complete prefix with each eligible
generated language noun and emits complete Native history office terms.
The documented highest-priest no-word fallback is "most high priest" or
"most high priests". Ordinary generated priest offices use the same noun
forms with their own prefixes. These inputs remain in the shared vocabulary;
this task does not run a generator or create a screenshot-title-only glossary.

For example, "Sacred Turquoise" is the title-cased form of the complete native
office "sacred turquoise". The existing sacred prefix and TURQUOISE noun sense
compose its translation, and the same source grammar covers the other native
prefix/noun combinations rather than naming a single photographed title.

Scope of native source extraction
----------------------------------
This renderer also sets native hover-tooltip ids for several icons. Actual
tooltip prose is constructed outside this renderer. Those ids are distinct
from text strings and are not classified here as renderer literals; the
existing complete tooltip sources and translations are recorded below.
The temple's direct textual output includes generated location/religion/deity
names, generated position titles, assigned names, all fixed branch captions,
numeric values, money glyphs, punctuation, editable values, and the cursor.
Sibling library, guildhall, tavern, and hospital literals are retained in
native-literal-sources.tsv so their shared-renderer provenance is explicit.

Hover tooltip source dependencies
----------------------------------
Existing source catalog: data/extracted/tooltip-sources.tsv.
Existing complete translations: data/runtime/tooltip-translations.tsv.
The source catalog stores the shared tooltip paragraph-vector address as
0x26fe370 + (tooltip_id * 24); each paragraph's native width is 24.
Its existing initializer addresses use that source catalog's address space,
not the renderer's reference PE RVA space used above. Exact source paragraphs
are normalized for repeated whitespace in the runtime translation file.

Renderer load 0x3b1ffa, tooltip ID 0x117, catalog paragraph 0x26ffd98:
  Source: Rename this location.
  Existing Chinese: 重命名此地点。
Renderer load 0x3b239a, tooltip ID 0x118, catalog paragraph 0x26ffdb0:
  Source: This option allows visitors from outside the fortress to enter this location.
  Existing Chinese: 此选项允许来自要塞外的访客进入此地点。
Renderer load 0x3b245c, tooltip ID 0x119, catalog paragraph 0x26ffdc8:
  Source: This option allows long-term residents of the fortress to enter this location.
  Existing Chinese: 此选项允许要塞的长期居民进入此地点。
Renderer load 0x3b251f, tooltip ID 0x11a, catalog paragraph 0x26ffde0:
  Source: This option indicates that the location is only open to fortress citizens.
  Existing Chinese: 此选项表示此地点仅对要塞公民开放。
Renderer load 0x3b25e8, tooltip ID 0x11b, catalog paragraph 0x26ffdf8:
  Source: This option indicates that the location is only open to members.
  Existing Chinese: 此选项表示此地点仅对成员开放。
Renderer load 0x3b8f94, tooltip ID 0x11c, catalog paragraph 0x26ffe10:
  Source: Remove this worker from this occupation.
  Existing Chinese: 解除此工人的这项职务。

Shared assigned-person row, 0x3b8551..0x3b8566, chooses tooltip ID 0x103
when unit.+0x11c has bit 0x400; otherwise it chooses 0x104:
ID 0x103, catalog paragraph 0x26ffbb8:
  Source: This worker is specialized and will only do tasks that match their workshop assignments, work details, and occupations.  Click to toggle.
  Existing Chinese: 此工人已设为专职，只会执行与其工坊分配、劳动分组和职务相符的任务。点击切换。
ID 0x104, catalog paragraph 0x26ffbd0:
  Source: This worker is not specialized and will do any free tasks that become available.  Click to toggle.
  Existing Chinese: 此工人未设为专职，会执行任何可接手的空闲任务。点击切换。

Shared assigned-person occupations, renderer 0x3b8787..0x3b87ed:
ID 0x105, catalog paragraph 0x26ffbe8:
  Source: This creature is a tavern keeper.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物担任酒保。
ID 0x106, catalog paragraph 0x26ffc00:
  Source: This creature is a performer.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物担任表演者。
ID 0x107, catalog paragraph 0x26ffc18:
  Source: This creature is a scholar.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物担任学者。
ID 0x108, catalog paragraph 0x26ffc30:
  Source: This creature is a scribe.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物担任抄写员。
ID 0x109, catalog paragraph 0x26ffc48:
  Source: This creature is a mercenary.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物担任佣兵。
ID 0x10a, catalog paragraph 0x26ffc60:
  Source: This creature is a monster slayer.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物担任怪物杀手。
ID 0x10b, catalog paragraph 0x26ffc78:
  Source: This creature is a doctor.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物担任医生。

Renderer loads 0x3b8a9f and 0x3b8c57, tooltip ID 0x10c,
catalog paragraph 0x26ffc90:
  Source: This creature is assigned to a specific workshop.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物被分配到指定工坊。
Renderer load 0x3b8df4, tooltip ID 0x10d, catalog paragraph 0x26ffca8:
  Source: This creature is assigned to a work detail.
  Existing Chinese: 此生物被分配到某项劳动分组。

Each tooltip paragraph above already has an entire-paragraph Chinese entry
in the existing runtime TSV. These paragraphs use the shared tooltip path;
they do not rely on the partial matching of the main detail row text.
